title: Closed [e] — é, -er, -ez, -ed, et, les/des/mes (set 7)
sounds: les / des / mes / tes / ses / ces
focus: All of these make the closed [e]: lips spread, tongue high, a pure « ay » with no glide at the end. It's spelled é; -er, -ez and -ed at the end of a word (parler, chez, pied); the word « et »; and the short words les, des, mes, tes, ses, ces. Exceptions: in a few short words the -er is [ɛʁ] with the r pronounced (mer, fer, hiver, cher, hier), and « est » has the open [ɛ]. Québécois keeps é and è clearly apart, even at the end of a word (« parlé » vs « parlait »).

sentences.fr: Il est tard, [et] il n'y a plus de lait.
sentences.en: It's late, and there's no more milk.

sentences.fr: Je vais au d[é]panneur au coin de la rue.
sentences.en: I go to the convenience store on the corner.

sentences.fr: J'achète du lait, d[es] œufs [et] un journal.
sentences.en: I buy milk, eggs and a newspaper.

sentences.fr: Le caissi[er] dit : « Vous pay[ez] comptant ? »
sentences.en: The cashier says: "Are you paying cash?"

sentences.fr: « Non, je vais pay[er] avec ma carte. Merci, bonne soir[é]e ! »
sentences.en: "No, I'll pay with my card. Thanks, have a good evening!"
